note: Outside the stated ICP on three of the four criteria that can be assessed. Income misses on liquidity rather than attitude — he says 'I don't have a problem with the amount' and means it, but he could not pay $6,000 or commit to $2,000 a month, his cash is tied up in estate taxes and pre-sale repairs, his credit score sits around 700 which the rep himself called 'a 50-50' for financing, and the money depends on third parties catching up on what they owe him. Good_to_great misses: by his own estimate he needs to lose 60-70lb, which is rescue rather than elevation, and note the setter's brief said 20-30lb — the file was carrying a materially wrong number until he corrected it on the call. Not_deconditioned misses on the exclusion as written, since 60-70lb overweight is past the threshold the ICP quote names, although it is only half true in spirit: he is emphatically not gym-averse, doing an hour of yoga six days a week, 10k steps, sauna and twice-daily meditation. Neglected_health is the one clear match and it is a strong one — no diagnosed disease, just a body that has absorbed six years of an unmanageable situation. `successful` is neither matched nor missed because occupation was never asked at any point in 62 minutes, which is itself a finding: the ICP's primary screen was not applied to this prospect at all. Worth carrying up alongside the Yannick call recorded in the same file, which is outside on four criteria — two consecutive calls on the same day, both well outside the stated definition, both booked by the setter pipeline and both taken to a full pitch.
